title: Pizza with Extra Cheese, Thick Crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with extra cheese and a thick crust is a classic Italian dish made from leavened dough, topped with tomato sauce, a generous layer of mozzarella and an additional cheese (often cheddar or parmesan). The crust is dense yet soft, while the cheese forms a golden, stretchy layer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original pizza originated in Naples in the 18th‑19th centuries, while thick‑crust styles are popular in the American “deep‑dish” tradition.
Cheese boosts calcium and protein content but also raises the calorie count.
Thick‑crust dough often contains more oil, giving the crust a crispier texture.
In the United States, extra‑cheese pizza ranks among the top‑10 most ordered items in chain restaurants.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that becomes more bioavailable after cooking.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Cheese provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium for bones
items.content: Mozzarella and cheddar are rich in calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough supplies B1, B2, and B3 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Cooked tomatoes increase lycopene availability, which may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain flour in the dough adds fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The abundance of cheese and dough makes the pizza energy‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheeses contain saturated fats that can raise cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Individuals sensitive to lactose may experience discomfort after eating.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese and sauce often contain a lot of salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into bite‑size slices. Fresh toppings such as vegetables, basil, or a drizzle of olive oil can add balance and freshness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore a crispy crust.
